chapter: Childhood and first music in Oklahoma
title: Oklahoma City, the Blue Devils and the Royal brothers
summary: He goes to Oklahoma City where the Blue Devils and Basie pass through; he clarifies he knew Wess and the Royals only from school and did not get along with Marshall.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: But then, after that, the gig... They were going further on up into Kansas, and I didn't know nothing about Kansas. So my brother told me, he said, "Let's go back to Muskogee." So I went back down there, and there wasn't no music happening down there, so I figured I'd better make tracks. So I went to Oklahoma City, where my other uncle, my father's sister lived, and I figured, well, maybe I could go there and stay there. And they had more music coming
through there, because they had the Blue Devils come through there, and Count Basie and all the guys were coming through. So I figured maybe I'd learn more there than I would anywhere else.
Now, when you knew Frank Wess and the Royal Brothers in Sapulpa...
Where did you know them? Just around, huh?
Just from going to school, yeah.
Yeah, going to school. But I mean, Frank and I, we've been friends all since that time. But Marshall and I never did get along too good, because he was older than I was, and I...
I guess he was older than everyone!

Yeah! Ha-ha-ha. Yeah, I'm going to tell him you said that. But he was; he was older. Ernie got along and Frank Wess and I got along, but Marshall and I didn't seem to hit it off, for some strange reason.
